output.brief: Cancelling RotaWeave would probably not fix this. The loss is concentrated at Dock Street and Westgate, where the app went live and the coordinator posts ended on 1 May. Millbrook has the app but kept its coordinator, and it is flat. Quarry Lane lost its coordinator but has no app, because the paper roster is still in use, and it is nearly flat. So it takes both changes together. The basic app has no recurring bookings. Coordinators used to book regulars into their usual slots, and that stopped on 1 May: bookings on behalf fell from 74 a week to 3. Regulars then lost their usual slots to new sign-ups. 88% of those who lost a slot twice or more are now inactive, against 11% of those who kept theirs. Callbacks say the same. Background checks are not the cause: 121 of 123 lapsed volunteers held a current check, and nearly all of the 23 deactivated in May came back. Commonplate recruitment explains almost nothing (2 of 61 callbacks). Low satisfaction is a symptom. What to do: at Dock Street and Westgate, assign someone to use the unused admin seat to pre-book regulars before each Thursday release, and phone lapsed volunteers to offer their slot back. Keep the background checks, because the county and insurer require them. Don't purge the inactive volunteers from the roster, and don't cancel the app. Check in again after 60 days. I'm fairly confident, though the callback sample is small.
